instructions.default:
## Instructions
- This is a conversation between you (the character) and the user.
- Use the **Knowledge retrieved** (from the workspace knowledge base) and **Memories retrieved** below as optional background.
- You choose what is relevant — you do not need to use all, or any, of it.
- source rank and score suggest the search relevancy of the knowledge item to the user message/context
- Answer **Last User Message** in your own style.

GraphPreferences.description:
Graphiti-backed temporal knowledge graph (the pivot from the earlier L3 graph slice).

``backend`` is the master switch: ``off`` = flat Qdrant only (today); ``graphiti``
= answer from graph facts; ``mix`` = fuse graph facts with Qdrant passages (the
recommended path, decision G4). Every other field is an admin-settable knob — no
hardcoded params. See docs/knowledge-graphiti-pivot-design.md §9–10.

backend.description: Master switch for knowledge retrieval. Off = today's flat Qdrant retrieval (graph untouched). Graphiti = answer from the graph's facts.
backend.title: Graph backend

extraction_profile.description: The AI profile Graphiti uses to read each chunk/turn and pull out entities + facts. Must be structured-output-capable; keep it deterministic. Empty uses Hiro's chat model.
extraction_profile.title: Graph extraction

small_profile.description: A cheaper AI profile for Graphiti's sub-steps — node dedupe, entity summaries, timestamps. Empty uses the graph extraction model.
small_profile.title: Graph small steps

embedder_profile.description: Embeds entity names and facts into the graph. Empty = the graph can't be built or searched. Locked once the graph holds data: another model needs a new graph.
embedder_profile.title: Embedding profile

temporal_default.description: Default time lens at retrieval. Current = only facts valid now (superseded facts hidden). Include historical = also surface invalidated facts. Overridable per query.
temporal_default.title: Temporal lens (default)

k_hop.description: Relationship hops out from matched entities when gathering related facts. 1 = direct neighbors only (precise); higher reaches further at more noise/cost.
k_hop.title: Expansion hops (k)

search_recipe.description: How candidates are ranked/fused WITHIN each leg (orthogonal to Search scope below). RRF = fast reciprocal-rank fusion (default). MMR = favors diversity. Cross-encoder = highest quality, slowest/most costly. MMR is not compatible with the episodes leg (BM25-only) — disabled when scope includes episodes.
search_recipe.title: Search recipe

search_scope.description: Which graph elements memory recall and knowledge retrieval READ from (orthogonal to Search recipe above). Edges = facts between entities (relations). Nodes = per-entity summaries (attribute-style memories, e.g. age, role, mood). Episodes = the raw conversation text of each saved turn — BM25 keyword match only (paraphrases may miss), useful as last-resort recall. "Edges + Episodes" keeps the raw turns but drops entity summaries (to test whether entity summaries are redundant with episodes).
search_scope.title: Search scope

entity_ontology.description: Which entity types extraction may use. Open = no predefined types; the model extracts freely (everything becomes a generic Entity) — broadest recall, captures activities, interests, media, and preferences. Typed = pin the 5-type vocabulary (Person / Place / Organization / Event / Object) — more precise, but drops first-person facts that don't fit those types. Changing this rebuilds the graph at the next ingest, so a re-ingest is required to take effect.
entity_ontology.title: Extraction ontology

custom_extraction_instructions.default: Capture first-person preferences, goals, habits and activities as facts even when only the speaker is named; treat the activity/topic/object as the second entity.
custom_extraction_instructions.description: Optional domain-generic guidance injected verbatim into Graphiti's entity + fact extraction prompts. Use it to steer what gets captured — e.g. capture first-person preferences, goals, habits and activities as facts even when only the speaker is named, treating the activity / topic / object as the second entity. Keep it generic (no dataset-specific rules). Blank = none. Applied at ingest, so a re-ingest is required to take effect.
custom_extraction_instructions.title: Extraction instructions

sim_min_score.description: Minimum cosine similarity (0–1) for a fact to even become a search candidate. Keep low (≈0.3) for recall — too high and paraphrased questions (e.g. asking 'wife' when the stored fact says 'married to') return no facts at all. Graphiti's own default is a strict 0.6. Precision belongs in the reranker's Min relevance below, not here.
sim_min_score.title: Candidate similarity floor

query_timeout_s.description: Hard ceiling on any single graph (Kuzu) query — writes, index rebuilds, and Graph-tab reads. Protects the server from a stuck index-rebuild checkpoint that can otherwise freeze the whole admin UI for minutes; a bounded failure is retried and logged instead. Keep above your slowest legitimate operation (index rebuilds take seconds). 0 = unlimited.
query_timeout_s.title: Query timeout (seconds)

observability.description: How much the graph engine records to Graph Runs (ingest + retrieval). Off = nothing — no ledger rows, tracer, or usage sinks (spares CPU; graph cost is NOT tracked). Ledger = one priced roll-up row per episode (ingest) and per search (rerank), so token cost still folds into the run total — the production default. Trace = Ledger plus a deep per-stage sidecar (the ⌗ retrieval/ingest trace dialogs) for debugging. Replaces the old Rich/Compact detail and the trace env vars.
observability.title: Graph observability

GraphPreferences.title: GraphPreferences

GraphViewPreferences.description:
Admin graph-VIZ display knobs for the shared Knowledge/Memories Graph tab.

Pure frontend-display settings: they tune how the force-graph view's per-node-type
filter dropdowns behave, NOT how facts are extracted, searched, or retrieved. The
graph engine ignores everything here.

large_type_threshold.description: In the Graph tab's per-type node filter, a type with more instances than this shows a 'many instances' performance heads-up in its dropdown. The dropdown still lists and searches every instance — this only flags very large types. Display-only.
large_type_threshold.title: Large node-type warning threshold

ImageProfile.description:
Named image-generation recipe: model + diffusion params + prompt scaffolding.

The scaffolding fields (``style_prefix`` / ``style_suffix``) wrap the caller's prompt
so a profile is a reusable *recipe*, not just numbers — the image analog of a voice
profile's style. ``size`` is a hint; fixed-resolution providers (flux-1-schnell:
1024x1024) ignore it. Hard limits (max steps, prompt length) live in the catalog and
are clamped by the provider implementation.
ImageProfile.title: ImageProfile

profile.description: The AI profile that answers from the knowledge base. Empty uses Hiro's chat model.
profile.title: Knowledge answering

rewrite_profile.description: The AI profile that rewrites a question into a search query (needs structured output; keep thinking off). Empty uses the knowledge answering model.
rewrite_profile.title: Knowledge query rewrite

prompt.default:
Use the provided knowledge context as your only source of facts; do not invent or assume anything that is not supported by it.

Answer every part of the question that the context supports. Partial answers are expected and welcome — never withhold a supported part just because another part is unsupported.

If a part of the question is not covered by the context, give the parts you can and briefly note what is missing. Do not reply with only 'I don't know' when any part of the question is supported by the context.
prompt.title: Answering prompt

respect_headings.description: Split chunks at markdown headings when ingesting documents.
respect_headings.title: Respect markdown headings

chunk_size.description: Target size per chunk at document ingest (characters).
chunk_size.title: Chunk size

chunk_overlap.description: Overlap between consecutive chunks. Must stay smaller than chunk size.
chunk_overlap.title: Chunk overlap

embed_structural_context.description: Prefix each chunk's embedded text with its document title and heading path so every chunk — including continuation pieces — carries its section context. Applies to new ingests; changing this requires re-ingesting existing documents.
embed_structural_context.title: Embed structural context

KnowledgeGraphRerankerPreferences.description:
Cross-encoder reranker for the graph fact-search leg.

Only takes effect when ``GraphPreferences.search_recipe == 'cross_encoder'``
(the admin UI greys this whole group out otherwise). ``profile`` names a reranker profile
(``rerank.profiles``: the model, and where a local one runs), resolved by the SAME
``resolve_reranker`` the flat Qdrant path uses — a local model that was never downloaded
fails fast, degrading the fact search to RRF (no silent fetch). Null = no reranker (RRF).

profile.description: The reranker profile that orders fact candidates. Empty = no reranker (the fact search falls back to RRF). Local models must be downloaded first.
profile.title: Reranker profile

min_relevance.description: Drop facts whose cross-encoder relevance is below this (0–1). 0 = keep all. Ignored by RRF/MMR.
min_relevance.title: Min relevance

KnowledgeGraphRerankerPreferences.title: KnowledgeGraphRerankerPreferences

embedder_profile.description: Embeds knowledge documents and questions. Empty = knowledge can't be indexed or searched. Locked once the collection holds documents.
embedder_profile.title: Embedding profile

KnowledgeRerankerPreferences.description:
Cross-encoder reranker over retrieved candidates (precision step).

Prefs-only, default off. ``profile`` names a reranker profile (``rerank.profiles``: a catalog
model or a local one, with its device and batch size), resolved by ``resolve_reranker`` to a
LangChain ``BaseDocumentCompressor``. Rerankers are dimensionless, so a swap is a hot config
change (no re-ingest). Null = no reranker (retrieval order used as-is) even when ``enabled``.

profile.description: The reranker profile that reorders retrieved candidates. Empty = no reranker. Local models must be downloaded first.
profile.title: Reranker profile

top_n.description: Final returned results if using rerank (top N).
top_n.title: Rerank results (top N)

KnowledgeRerankerPreferences.title: KnowledgeRerankerPreferences

top_k.description: Fused results from hybrid search or direct results from dense only search (after applying minimum score).
top_k.title: Search/fused results (top K)

min_score.description: Applies only to dense (Vector search) branch.
min_score.title: Minimum score (Dense only)

prefetch_limit.description: Results to return for dense (Vector) or sparse (BM25) separately, before RRF fusion (Hybrid Only).
prefetch_limit.title: Candidates per branch

prompt.default:
Rewrite the user's question into one clean, standalone search query.

Fix typos and normalize informal or dialectal phrasing into clear formal language, but do NOT change the meaning or add information that is not in the question.

If a conversation is provided, resolve references (pronouns, 'the second one', 'his brother') against it so the query stands alone without the conversation.

Copy proper nouns, names, dates, and identifiers VERBATIM into `keywords` — never translate or 'correct' a name.

Set `knowledge_needed` to false when the message is just a greeting, farewell, thanks, acknowledgement, or small talk and clearly does not ask for stored information; otherwise true. Do not invent facts or answer the question.

Respond with a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
- `standalone_query` (string): the rewritten standalone search query.
- `keywords` (array of strings): proper nouns, names, dates, and identifiers copied verbatim.
- `knowledge_needed` (boolean): false only for greetings/thanks/small talk, otherwise true.
- `entities` (array of strings): named entities the question asks about (people, places, organizations) and qualified relational mentions like 'my sister' or 'mom'; empty when the question references no specific entity (e.g. 'what is photosynthesis?').
prompt.title: Query Rewrite Prompt

default_on.title: Enable Query Rewrite on Ask Tab

LLMPreferences.description:
Which catalog models to use when the workspace has credentials for them, and the AI profiles
of Hiro's chat and reading pictures.

Phase 7b step 5: ``default_chat`` + ``default_tuning_profile`` became ``chat_profile`` (one AI
profile), ``IMAGE_VISION_MODEL`` became ``vision_profile``, and ``default_tts`` moved to voice
profiles (``voice.hiro_profile``). No backward compatibility: v3 files are converted once
(``convert_v4``).

chat_profile.description: The AI profile Hiro chats with (and the model the other jobs borrow when their own profile isn't set). A character's own AI profiles come first.
chat_profile.title: Hiro's chat

vision_profile.description: The AI profile that describes pictures sent to Hiro. Empty = pictures aren't read.
vision_profile.title: Reading pictures

http_keepalive_s.description: How long idle HTTPS connections to model providers (OpenAI, DeepSeek) are kept warm before closing. Larger avoids a TLS handshake on the first call of each chat turn (~1s). Effective ceiling is the provider's own idle timeout (~60-240s). Takes effect on server restart.
http_keepalive_s.title: Provider connection keepalive (seconds)

request_timeout_s.description: How long to wait for a cloud model provider to answer (or to send the next part of a streamed answer) before that attempt counts as failed. Applies to chat and speech-to-text on every cloud provider. Takes effect on server restart.
request_timeout_s.title: Provider response timeout (seconds)

max_retries.description: How many times a failed or timed-out cloud model call (provider overloaded, rate limited, network error) is retried before the error is reported. 0 = no retry. Takes effect on server restart.
max_retries.title: Provider retries

LLMPreferences.title: LLMPreferences

LocalServerSettings.description: How the core loads models on a local server (Part B, ported from HomeHiro's ModelSetup).
LocalServerSettings.title: LocalServerSettings

MemoryExtractionPreferences.description: Whether — and how — the agent stores new long-term memories after a reply (memory_out).

enabled.title: Remember new facts after each reply

window_turns.description: Conversation turns (user+agent exchanges) accumulated into one memory episode before extraction. 1 = ingest every turn; higher batches more turns into a richer episode.
window_turns.title: Turns per memory batch

chunk_min_tokens.description: Token budget for a batched memory episode. A window over this sheds turns to fit (a lone oversized turn is trimmed). Keep at/below Graphiti's chunk threshold so an episode is never re-split.
chunk_min_tokens.title: Max tokens per memory episode

session_gap_minutes.description: If the next message arrives more than this many minutes after the previous one, the pending turns are ingested as a finished session and a new batch starts.
session_gap_minutes.title: New-session gap (minutes)

idle_flush_hours.description: A background sweep ingests a conversation's pending turns after this many hours of inactivity, so an abandoned conversation's memories still land.
idle_flush_hours.title: Idle flush (hours)

instructions.default: This text is a chat transcript. In it, "{user}" is the human user and "{character}" is the AI assistant/character; each line is prefixed with its speaker and timestamp. Extract facts ONLY about {user}, and only as {user} stated or explicitly confirmed them. Treat {character}'s lines purely as context for resolving what {user} refers to — never record a fact asserted by {character} that {user} did not state or confirm.
instructions.description: Guidance appended to the graph fact-extractor when ingesting chat memory (a two-speaker window). Default: attribute facts to the user only, treating the assistant's lines as context. Use {user} / {character} placeholders — they are filled with the actual speaker names at ingest. Applies to conversation memory only — not knowledge.
instructions.title: Memory extraction instructions

MemoryExtractionPreferences.title: MemoryExtractionPreferences

MemoryPreferences.description:
Agent memory settings — a thin feature layer over the shared Graphiti graph engine.

Gated purely by ``enabled``; the engine (extraction model, embedder, search) comes from
the top-level ``graph`` preferences, and ``create_memory_service`` degrades to ``None``
when that engine can't be built. The mem0-legacy model / embedder / reranker fields are
gone (mem0 → Graphiti, Phase 5).
MemoryPreferences.title: MemoryPreferences

max_elements_per_kind.title: Max elements / kind

max_fact_chars.title: Max fact chars
